inline_comments.comment: Same inconsistency as in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/edges.js`: `createLabel` is called with `startEdgeLabelRight` as the parent, but the element is immediately moved to `inner`. Pass `inner` directly and remove the redundant `inner.node().appendChild(startLabelElement)` call to match the pattern used by the other three terminal label blocks.

In the `endLabelLeft` block, `createLabel(inner, ...)` appends the element to `inner`, then `inner.attr('transform', ...)` is set to center the element, but the very next line `endEdgeLabelLeft.node().appendChild(endLabelElement)` moves the element *out of* `inner` into `endEdgeLabelLeft`. Since the label is no longer a descendant of `inner`, the centering transform on `inner` has no effect on its position.

This is a pre-existing bug carried forward by this PR, and it affects both `endLabelLeft` and `endLabelRight` in both `edges.js` files. `startLabelLeft` is the only terminal label block that correctly leaves the element inside `inner`. The spurious `appendChild` calls should be removed, or the transform should be applied to `endEdgeLabelLeft` instead. Since this PR already touches all four blocks, it is the right moment to fix the pre-existing cases.

When `width === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (as passed by the new `createLabel`), `max-width` and `text-align: center` are no longer applied to the HTML label `<div>`. Previously, `createLabel`'s HTML path always produced a centered label. With `display: table-cell` and no explicit `text-align`, text defaults to `start` (left-aligned), which will visually change existing diagrams that used `createLabel` with HTML labels.

If the intent is "no width constraint but still center the text", consider applying `text-align: center` unconditionally and only gating `max-width`.

The JSDoc comment says *"splits on spaces for words"* but the implementation uses `\s` (all Unicode whitespace, including tabs, non-breaking spaces, etc.), not just literal space characters. Update the comment to say *"splits on whitespace"* for accuracy.

The TODO comment `// TODO: Doesn't this need an \`await\`?` is left in production code and identifies a real runtime bug (see the separate defect comment on the `createLabel` call). TODO comments that flag known defects should be resolved before merging, not committed.

The new comment `// TODO: the createText function returns a \`Promise\`, so I'm guessing it never runs?` is left unresolved. If `createText` is not awaited in the markdown branch, the Promise is silently discarded and the label never renders — this should be verified and fixed (add `await`) rather than left as a speculative TODO.

general_comments.comment: The changeset in `.changeset/olive-mails-joke.md` is marked `patch`, but this PR adds net-new capabilities to labels (KaTeX rendering and FontAwesome icon-pack support) that previously did not exist in the `createLabel` code path. Per project conventions, additive features should use a `minor` bump, not `patch`.

The image-loading logic in `configureLabelImages` was extracted from two nearly identical copies in `shapes/util.ts` and `dagre-wrapper/shapes/util.js` — good deduplication. However, the `.js` version in `dagre-wrapper/shapes/util.js` was updated to call the new utility via an import from `rendering-util/rendering-elements/shapes/labelImageUtils.ts`. Consider whether importing across the `dagre-wrapper` ↔ `rendering-util` boundary is the right layering, or whether the utility should live at a path accessible to both (e.g., `packages/mermaid/src/utils.ts`).

In `nonMarkdownToLines`, splitting each line on `\s` produces an empty-string token (`{ content: '', type: 'normal' }`) for each run of whitespace, including leading whitespace. `updateTextContentAndStyles` renders the first token without a leading space and subsequent tokens with one prepended space, so consecutive whitespace and leading spaces in a label are not faithfully preserved. The old `createLabel` SVG path used `row.trim()` to normalize this, so behavior is broadly equivalent, but it may be worth documenting the normalization assumption or applying `.filter(Boolean)` to the word array to drop empty tokens and avoid generating no-op tspans.
